business_flow: User interacts with a web shop API (addresses, basket, products, payments, cards, feedbacks, captcha, chatbot, rest endpoints). Many endpoints accept authenticated requests (Authorization Bearer token or cookie token).
thought_process: Per mandate: examine each HTTP entry and only produce findings where evidence in the traffic shows a possible business-logic abuse according to the five checks. I will only report endpoints where the request/response content demonstrates a potential BLV.

I will produce one finding per vulnerable endpoint. Each finding must include category (BLA code mapping to provided list), description referencing evidence_entry_ids (the HAR entry number(s)), severity, and reproduction_guide with payload_mutation and exact curl_command placeholders.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Potential Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) on GET /api/Addresss/{id} (entry #5). The traffic shows GET /api/Addresss/7 returning 200 while Authorization token corresponds to user id 23. Because the endpoint uses a numeric id and the request returns 200, this indicates the API may allow retrieving address id 7 directly based on the path without explicit evidence of ownership enforcement. If address id 7 belongs to the same user it's fine; but the pattern (numeric direct reference plus many other address operations on /api/Addresss/{id}) suggests possible IDOR. Evidence: request path exposes object id and server returned 200.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change the URL path id to another target id (e.g., change /api/Addresss/7 to /api/Addresss/{{target_id}}) to attempt access to another user's address.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Object State Manipulation: POST/PUT /api/Addresss (entries #4, #6) allow client to set address fields directly (country, fullName, mobileNum, zipCode, streetAddress, city, state). Critical state (address ownership) may be set or modified by client; POST returns 201 and PUT returns 200 for /api/Addresss/7. If the API trusts provided AddressId or allows setting arbitrary UserId elsewhere, attackers could manipulate address ownership. Evidence: POST /api/Addresss/ (entry #4) created an address; PUT /api/Addresss/7 (entry #6) updated address 7.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Use PUT to /api/Addresss/{{target_id}} and change fields (e.g., modify 'fullName' from 'home' to 'attacker' or change 'mobileNum') to see if updates are accepted for addresses not owned by the user.
reproduction_guide.curl_command: curl -i -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer {{auth_token}}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"country":"Indonesia","fullName":"attacker","mobileNum":6277711122,"zipCode":"144444","streetAddress":"Attacker St","city":"Bandung","state":"Jawa Barat"}' "http://localhost:3000/api/Addresss/{{target_id}}"

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Potential IDOR on GET/PUT/DELETE /api/BasketItems/{id} (entries #11, #12, #13). The traffic shows DELETE /api/BasketItems/9 returned 200, GET /api/BasketItems/9 returned 200, and PUT /api/BasketItems/9 returned 200. The endpoint uses numeric direct references for basket items. This pattern suggests the API may permit direct access/manipulation by id without strict ownership checks.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Attempt to GET/PUT/DELETE another basket item id by changing path /api/BasketItems/9 to /api/BasketItems/{{target_id}}.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: State manipulation on POST /api/BasketItems (entries #9, #10) — client supplies 'BasketId' and 'quantity' when adding items. The request shows 'BasketId': "6" provided by client. If BasketId is trusted from client rather than determined server-side from session, attacker can add items to arbitrary baskets or escalate quantities. Evidence: both POST requests include BasketId and quantity in body and succeeded (200).

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'BasketId' from '6' to another basket id (e.g., 7) or change 'quantity' to an inflated value (e.g., 999) in POST /api/BasketItems.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Payment/workflow bypass possibility: POST /rest/basket/6/checkout (entry #63) accepts 'couponData' and orderDetails (paymentId, addressId, deliveryMethodId) and returned 200. The client supplies paymentId ("7") and addressId ("7"). If the API trusts paymentId without validating payment completion, an attacker could set paymentId to an arbitrary id (e.g., a free payment or an already-paid id) to bypass actual payment. Evidence: checkout payload includes client-supplied paymentId and couponData.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'orderDetails.paymentId' to another id (e.g., '0' or another payment id) or supply couponData tampered value to attempt to complete checkout without valid payment.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Shadow endpoint files accessible under /ftp (entries #53, #54). A GET to /ftp/order_b783-167bf60f01c1a3bb.pdf (entry #54) returned 200, indicating presence of an FTP-like directory exposed over HTTP. This appears to be an undocumented artifact (order PDF) accessible by guessing path. This is a shadow endpoint / file exposure.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Request other files in /ftp by changing filename portion to other known order ids (e.g., change order_b783-...pdf to order_b{{target_id}}.pdf).

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Internal state disclosure in Authorization JWT content shown in request headers across many entries (e.g., entry #3). The Bearer token decoded content in logs includes internal fields like 'totpSecret', 'deluxeToken', 'isActive', lastLoginIp, createdAt/updatedAt etc. Presence of long token in cookie and Authorization header and repeated echo in HAR suggests internal sensitive state may be leakable or predictable. Evidence: Authorization header in entry #3 contains JWT with many internal claims.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Inspect Authorization header and decode the JWT token claims; no request mutation required.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Shadow/undocumented admin REST endpoints observed under /rest/admin/* (entries #58, #59, #60). The traffic includes GET /rest/admin/application-configuration and /rest/admin/application-version returning 304, indicating admin configuration endpoints are present and reachable (possibly without strict access verification). These are likely shadow functions intended for admin use.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Attempt to access /rest/admin/application-configuration or other /rest/admin endpoints using your token; change path to other admin resources.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Workflow order bypass / missing transition validation: REST deluxe membership flow: GET /rest/deluxe-membership returned 400 while POST /rest/deluxe-membership with {'paymentMode':'card','paymentId':7} returned 200 (entries #79, #80). The client supplies paymentId and obtains success. If the server accepts arbitrary paymentId and activates membership without verifying gateway payment result, users can bypass proper payment flows. Evidence: POST accepted client-supplied paymentId and returned 200.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: POST to /rest/deluxe-membership with 'paymentId' set to an arbitrary or zero value to test whether membership is granted without actual payment.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: State Manipulation: PUT /rest/wallet/balance (entry #107) accepts 'balance' and 'paymentId' to set wallet balance. The request shows a client-side provided 'balance': 555 and 'paymentId': 7 and returned 200. Allowing clients to update wallet balance via this endpoint is dangerous if server does not validate paymentId or that the requester is authorized to change the balance. Evidence: PUT accepted a balance update payload and succeeded.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'balance' to a large value (e.g., 999999) or set 'paymentId' to arbitrary id to see if wallet balance is modified without payment verification.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Shadow endpoints under /rest/chatbot/* (entries #69-76) allow actions like 'respond', 'setname' and return 200. Chatbot endpoints expose functionality (including stateful 'setname') that appears to accept arbitrary actions. These may be undocumented or provide admin-like capabilities. Evidence: multiple POST /rest/chatbot/respond with 'action' values and GET /rest/chatbot/status show accessible endpoints.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: POST to /rest/chatbot/respond changing 'action' to 'setname' or other action (e.g., change 'query' to exfiltrate data) to see if chatbot state changes or responds with sensitive info.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Internal State Disclosure via cookies: 'continueCode' cookie is present and reused across requests (seen in entries #33, #48, #52, #66, #97, #82, #96). The continueCode likely encodes workflow state which may allow session continuation or bypass if predictable. This cookie being visible suggests internal workflow state is stored client-side. Evidence: cookie continueCode=Yy2xK6... appears in multiple requests and responses.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Capture and replay or modify the 'continueCode' cookie value in subsequent requests to endpoints that use it (e.g., /api/Quantitys or /rest/products/search) to see if workflow or access can be manipulated.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: State Manipulation / Resource quota: POST /api/Recycles/ (entry #36) shows client supplies 'quantity': 10 in body for recycle action. If quantity affects resource allocation or credits and server accepts arbitrary 'quantity' without validation or quota checks, attacker can request excessive resources. Evidence: POST recycle accepted 'quantity':10 returning 201.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: POST to /api/Recycles/ with 'quantity' set to a very large number (e.g., 9999) or change AddressId to another user's address to test validation.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: State Manipulation: POST /api/Cards/ (entry #15) accepts full card details including expYear 2080 and cardNum 1111234455555555. The server returned 201, indicating card addition accepted. If card tokenization/validation is weak or client-controlled, attackers could add arbitrary card records for use in payments. Evidence: POST /api/Cards/ returned 201 for provided data.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: POST to /api/Cards/ with arbitrary cardNum and long expiry (e.g., expYear 2099) and see if card is stored for payments.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Missing Transition Validation: POST /api/Complaints/ (entry #21) includes 'UserId': 23 in request body. If server trusts provided UserId rather than deriving from auth token, an attacker can create complaints on behalf of other users. Evidence: request body includes UserId set by client and response 201.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'UserId' from 23 to another user id (e.g., 24) in POST /api/Complaints/ to attempt to create complaint for another user.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: State Manipulation: POST /api/Feedbacks/ (entry #27 and #26 shows listing) allows client to supply 'UserId', 'captchaId', 'captcha', 'comment', and 'rating' and returned 201. If server trusts supplied UserId rather than authenticated identity, attacker can post feedback on behalf of other users or manipulate ratings. Evidence: POST payload includes 'UserId': 23 and response 201.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'UserId' to another id or manipulate 'rating' to maximum and POST to /api/Feedbacks/ to see if allowed.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Potential IDOR on GET /api/Cards/{id} (entry #16). The request GET /api/Cards/7 returned 200; the endpoint uses numeric id and card data is sensitive. If no ownership validation, one user could access another user's card metadata. Evidence: GET /api/Cards/7 returned 200 with Authorization header set.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change path id to another card id: /api/Cards/{{target_id}} to attempt to read other users' cards.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: State Manipulation: POST /api/BasketItems/ (entry #9) includes ProductId and BasketId. If malicious client can create items in arbitrary baskets, they can inject items or manipulate basket totals. Evidence: request body includes BasketId="6" and succeeded.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Change 'BasketId' to another value and 'quantity' to a high number to manipulate basket.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Shadow endpoint /rest/2fa and /rest/2fa/status accessible (entries #56, #57). These endpoints may expose two-factor authentication admin or debug status. Entry shows GET /rest/2fa and GET /rest/2fa/status returned 200/0, indicating presence of 2FA endpoints that may be undocumented.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Access /rest/2fa/status to view 2FA state or attempt to toggle via other /rest/2fa endpoints.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Internal State Disclosure: Many Authorization headers include JWTs with identity and internal flags (entries multiple e.g., #5, #7, #12). These tokens include user metadata (isActive, totpSecret empty, deluxeToken etc.) which can reveal internal application state. Evidence: repeated Authorization header values present in requests/responses.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Decode the Authorization Bearer token locally to inspect contained claims.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Shadow endpoints under /rest/image-captcha and /rest/captcha accessible (entries #67-68, #81-82). These endpoints expose captcha artifacts (image endpoints). Their presence may allow automated bypass or reuse of captcha tokens if not bound to session. Evidence: GET /rest/captcha/ and /rest/image-captcha/ returned 200.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Request /rest/image-captcha/ and reuse returned captcha id or image across sessions to test whether captcha validation is tied to session.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Sequence Bypass potential via /rest/basket/{id}/coupon and /rest/basket/{id}/checkout (entries #64, #65, #63). The coupon endpoint exists and PUT /rest/basket/6/coupon/6665434535 returned 404, but checkout accepted couponData in body. If coupon application can be bypassed or checkout accepts arbitrary couponData without validation, workflow can be bypassed. Evidence: checkout accepted 'couponData' in request body (entry #63).

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Supply manipulated couponData in checkout (e.g., couponData set to another code) or skip coupon endpoint and submit checkout directly.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: State manipulation: POST /rest/memories (entries #85-86) accepts file upload (multipart/form-data) and returns 200. The endpoint allows uploading arbitrary memory images. If memory records are associated with UserId specified in headers/body (not shown) or if uploads affect quotas, lack of server-side validation may permit resource abuse. Evidence: POST with image payload returned 200 and cookies include continueCode.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Upload large file/multiple files to /rest/memories to test quota enforcement.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: State manipulation: POST /rest/memories (entry #86) used multipart form to upload image named 'memory' without additional metadata; accepted and returned 200. If memory entries are processed trustingly, attacker may store arbitrary content. Evidence: large multipart payload accepted.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Upload content with crafted metadata/filenames to /rest/memories to attempt to embed harmful content or exceed storage quotas.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: State Manipulation via /rest/wallet/balance GET/PUT (entries #105-107). GET /rest/wallet/balance returned 304; PUT accepted balance updates. If wallet balance can be updated via client-supplied paymentId (entry #107), this is direct manipulation of financial state. Evidence: PUT with balance 555 and paymentId 7 returned 200.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Call PUT /rest/wallet/balance with a large 'balance' and an arbitrary 'paymentId' to see if account balance increases.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: Potential IDOR on /rest/track-order/{orderToken} (entries #98, #99, #54). The application serves order PDFs under /ftp/order_{token}.pdf and /rest/track-order/{token} returned 304 for token b783-167bf60f01c1a3bb. If tracking uses an unprotected token that can be guessed, another user may access order details. Evidence: /ftp/order_b783-...pdf (entry #54) returned 200 and /rest/track-order/{token} returned 304.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Request /rest/track-order/{{target_token}} or /ftp/order_{{target_token}}.pdf where {{target_token}} is altered to guess other orders.

potential_vulnerabilities.description: State Manipulation: PUT /api/Addresss/7 (entry #6) allowed update of 'fullName' from 'home' to 'homee' and returned 200. This shows clients can change address records through API calls. If no ownership check, can be abused. Evidence: PUT to /api/Addresss/7 with changed data returned 200.

reproduction_guide.payload_mutation: Perform PUT /api/Addresss/{{target_id}} and change fields to observe update acceptance.
reproduction_guide.curl_command: curl -i -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer {{auth_token}}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"country":"Indonesia","fullName":"changed","mobileNum":6277711133,"zipCode":"144444","streetAddress":"New St","city":"Bandung","state":"Jawa Barat"}' "http://localhost:3000/api/Addresss/{{target_id}}"
